name: repeat_routine_calls_countdown
description: Counts from the given value down to zero, calling one fixed unnamed routine on each step, and then calls that same routine once more. The routine is unnamed in the executable, so its own behaviour is not described here.

name: store_word_in_global
description: Stores its 16-bit argument into a shared global variable and returns. It is called from one unnamed routine.

name: store_word_in_global
description: Stores its 16-bit argument into a shared global variable and returns. It was executed in the reference run, but no callers are recorded for it.

name: write_four_bytes_table_entry
description: Multiplies its first argument by eight to select an eight-byte table entry, then stores four byte arguments into the first four bytes of that entry in order.

name: store_two_bytes_indexed_entry
description: Uses the shared global variable, scaled by eight, as an index into an eight-byte-per-entry table and stores two byte arguments into the first two bytes of that entry. Two unnamed routines call it.

name: set_low_nibble_table_entry
description: Uses the shared global variable, scaled by eight, to select a table entry, then replaces the low four bits of its third byte with the low nibble of its argument while keeping the high four bits.

name: read_first_byte_table_entry
description: Returns the first byte of the table entry selected by the shared global variable, scaled by eight. It is called from one unnamed routine.

name: read_second_byte_table_entry
description: Returns the second byte of the table entry selected by the shared global variable, scaled by eight. It is called from one unnamed routine.

name: assemble_file_path_name
description: Builds a path string into a buffer from up to four optional parts: the first part is followed by a colon when the buffer does not already end in one, the second is preceded by a separator character from a shared global variable unless the buffer already ends in a backslash, slash or colon, the third is appended as is, and the fourth is introduced by a period. Each part is appended by a called unnamed copy routine.

name: append_string_to_buffer
description: Scans the destination string to its terminating zero and then copies the source string, including its terminator, starting at that point. It returns the original destination pointer.

name: divide_signed_32bit_values
description: Divides a signed 32-bit dividend by a signed 32-bit divisor. A negative dividend makes it call a helper routine and return the negated result, a negative divisor makes it return the helper's result unchanged, and otherwise it shifts the operands to normalise the divisor and divides in 16-bit steps.

name: normalize_fixed_point_divide
description: Divides a 32-bit dividend by a 32-bit divisor. If the divisor fits in its low word it uses two direct 16-bit divisions; otherwise it shifts the operands to normalise the divisor, estimates the quotient and corrects it. The result is a packed 64-bit value with the quotient in its upper part and the remainder in its lower part.

name: multiply_32bit_words
description: Multiplies two 32-bit values by forming 16-bit partial products: the two cross products of the high and low words are summed and shifted into the high half, and the low-word product is added. It returns the 32-bit product.

name: copy_string_return_terminator
description: Copies a null-terminated source string into a destination buffer, including the terminating zero. It returns the address in the destination where that terminating zero was written.

name: store_self_address_then_trap
description: Stores the address of this routine into a shared global variable, then executes trap instruction zero before returning. It is the first routine in its segment.

name: stub_return_immediately
description: Contains only a return and does nothing. It is reached through an address taken elsewhere in the segment, is called from a small neighbouring routine, and was executed in the reference run.

name: configure_display_and_copper
description: Writes display window, data fetch and bitplane control hardware registers and the interrupt enable register, and references the text ultimav. It calls a copper-list starter, a jump-table entry and one unnamed routine. No pseudo-code is available, so this is based only on the registers, text and calls.

name: manage_interrupts_and_sprites
description: Accesses the interrupt enable and request registers in both their read and write forms, and touches the eight sprite pointer registers. It calls a copper-list starter and a small two-instruction routine, and its pseudo-code tests bit flags in a shared global variable to decide how far to proceed.

name: stub_return_immediately
description: Contains only a return and does nothing. It is a single-instruction stub in a small runtime segment and was executed in the reference run.

name: start_loader_code_region
description: Describes a four-instruction block at the start of the loader's raw code file. No pseudo-code is available because the decompiler timed out, so its purpose is not determined from this evidence.

name: configure_display_and_ports
description: Writes the bitplane modulo, display window, data fetch and bitplane control registers and the interrupt enable register, and touches the controller port register that carries the fire buttons and disk status. It is the opening block of the ultimav raw code file and calls two unnamed routines; no pseudo-code is available.

name: start_copper_list_dma
description: Writes the copper list pointer register, strobes the copper jump register so the list starts at once, and writes the DMA control register. It is four instructions long and is called by a small routine in the same file.

name: configure_four_audio_channels
description: Writes the location and volume registers of all four audio channels and the DMA control register, and touches the controller port register that carries the fire buttons and disk status. It calls three unnamed routines; no pseudo-code is available, so the body of 122 instructions is not described in detail.

name: program_audio_sample_channels
description: Writes the sample location and length registers of all four audio channels and the DMA control register, and touches the first custom-chip register. It calls two unnamed routines; no pseudo-code is available, so the sample handling is not described.

name: process_undescribed_routine_block
description: No pseudo-code is available for this 65-instruction routine, and no hardware registers or referenced text are recorded for it. It has two unnamed callers, so its purpose is not determined from this evidence.

name: invoke_two_unnamed_routines
description: Calls two unnamed routines and is itself called from two unnamed routines. No pseudo-code is available for its 96-instruction body, so nothing further is recorded about its behaviour.
